newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firm amid NY line outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firm amid NY line outage.

text.p: Spot prices of wholesale electricity in the northeastern U.S. stayed firm Tuesday amid outage of a high-voltage transmission line that moves power from western to central and southern New York state.
"Prices were not running up or down," said a marketer in Houston.
The outage of the line, operated by Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, reduced capacity of the "Central-East Interface" by 1,000 megawatts (MW). The transfer point usually has a capacity of 2,600-2,700 MW.
Eastern and southern New York utilities needed to switch on expensive fossil-fired generation to make up for reduced supply from western New York and Canada, marketers said.

Central Hudson Gas & Electric Co fired up a 600 MW unit at its oil-fired Roseton facility at the request of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) to insure transmission stability in the southeastern part of the power grid.
The maintenance shutdown of the 345 kilovolt (KV) line, which runs between Utica and Albany, began Monday and was planned to stay down until Friday.
Today's rebound in the NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures failed to extend Monday's rise since residual fuel oil became cheaper to use than gas at the burner tip this month, marketers said.
In the eastern portion of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday remained at $31.00-$33.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).
Off-peak, non-firm power for Wednesday in eastern NYPP was again quoted at $19.00-$20.00.
In the western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Tuesday held steady at $19.00-$20.00 amid greater spot supply in the western part of the grid due to the east-west transmission constraint.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Wednesday remained at $14.00-$15.00.

Spot power prices in the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday at the Northeast Utilities border was quoted at $34.00-$36.00, a wider range than $35.00-$36.00 Monday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Wednesday delivery to the NU border was quoted at $18.00-$21.00, off from Monday's $21.00-$22.00.
Vermont Yankee Power Corp continued to hold output at its 510 MW Vermont Yankee plant at 80 percent of capacity while repairing a condensate pump seal leak.
In eastern Canada, next-day power for peak deiivery at the Quebec-New Brunswick border was assessed near $23.00 and for off-peak delivery near $16.00, marketers said.

Wednesday's temperatures in much of the Northeast were predicted to peak in 30s Fahrenheit and bottom in the 20s. A cooling trend was forecast Friday with temperaturees falling one to three degrees below normal
